title: Feature: Spend caps and budget governor (adversarial: loop, retry storm, fan-out)
evidence: bun test test/cost.test.ts 6 pass/0 fail; test/cost-adversarial.test.ts 5 pass/0 fail; test/phase2 56 pass/0 fail; test/phase6 89 pass/0 fail. Mutation: governor.record(0 on error) => exactly 2 fail (a FAILED attempt is charged..., RETRY STORM...), reverted to 0 occurrences of MUTANT
notes: Acceptance bun test test/cost.test.ts plus the adversarial cases the task names (loop, retry storm, fan-out). Loop already pinned in test/cost.test.ts; fan-out already pinned twice (test/phase2/reservations.test.ts racing-process property + test/phase6/worker-budget.test.ts 5 workers vs root cap). The gap was the RETRY STORM: nothing pinned that a failed attempt settles a conservative estimate rather than zero, so a provider erroring on every call could have retried for free forever. Added test/cost-adversarial.test.ts (5 tests): success settles exact provider usage; a failed attempt is charged the full reserve (not zero, not a guess in our favour); a storm of failures exhausts the cap and never exceeds it; a settlement persistence failure propagates instead of becoming a free retry; an unpriced model is refused before any request leaves the process. PROVEN TO BITE: mutating model-accounting.ts to settle 0 on error kills exactly the 2 guarding tests (3 still pass), then reverted. Desktop parity is by construction - the Budget screen reads engine numbers via desktop/src/engine/budget.ts readEngineBudget() -> GET /budget and never recomputes spend; tighteningPatch is covered in test/desktop/selection-accounting.test.ts.

title: Feature: Security plane (policy gate, approvals, secret broker, tamper-evident audit)
evidence: bun test test/security/ 377 pass 0 fail; test/trust 159 pass 0 fail; mutation chain.valid->true => (fail) Phase 4 tamper matrix (a) single-entry edit breaks chain replay, 10 pass 1 fail; reverted (0 occurrences of MUTANT)
notes: Security plane verified with the existing suites rather than new prose: test/security 377 pass/0 fail (policy/ACL, canonical-bypass, exec-integrity, filesystem authority+implicit+index-context+native-flags, MCP allowlist+description-poison+pinning, egress proxy, audit crypto/anchor/signer, phase31 buckets) and test/trust 159 pass/0 fail (isolation, namespaces, process bounds). The tamper-evident claim was not taken on trust: the Phase 4 tamper matrix already edits a single audit entry and asserts chainValid=false + signaturesValid=false, and separately performs the F-08 wholesale truncate + consistent hash rebuild attack that only the signed head catches. I mutation-proved it - forcing verifyCrypto() to report the chain valid (chain.valid -> true in workspace-store.ts) kills exactly (a) single-entry edit breaks chain replay and leaves the other 10 green, then reverted. No security control was weakened to make a test pass.
